diagram_math_checks.objects: I=Id₂, full cone C=R², null cone C₀={(t,0):t≥0}, z=(2,3/2), p_C=z, p₀=(2,0).
diagram_math_checks.check: Both cones are nonempty, closed, convex, contain zero and satisfy C₀⊆C, as required by the Statement. Choosing C=R² is compatible with the full parameter set being open and the local full sets closed.

By the Fisher-distance definition and Fact F2, I=Id₂ makes squared distance Euclidean. For (t,0) in C₀, squared distance from z is (t-2)²+9/4, minimized at admissible t=2. Thus p₀=(2,0), the dashed segment has length 3/2 and is perpendicular to C₀. Since z belongs to R², p_C=z and d_I(z,C)=0.

The label 9/4 equals d_I²(z,C₀)-d_I²(z,C)=(3/2)²-0, with the subtraction order exactly as in the Statement and proof step 4.1. Nonnegativity agrees with nested sets. The right-pointing ray represents all nonnegative t; coordinate arrows are axes, not additional cone boundaries.

The figure illustrates a fixed sample point only; it does not claim to prove local convergence, the uniform expansion, tightness, or the distributional limit. The original rigorous proof is unchanged and independent of the figure.
